tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
Intersection over Union (IoU) score, Detected branch ratio (DBR), Detected length ratio (DLR), Precision, Running
time, Airway leakages. the airway leakage is actually the modified false positive rate of the airway predictions,
which is a through AL=FP/(TP+FN).


The evaluation code can be found at https://github.com/Nandayang/FANN-for-airwaysegmentation/
tree/main/utils

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.


 Airway-Informed Quantitative CT Imaging Biomarker for Fibrotic Lung Disease

IoU, Precision, airway leakage aim to assess the comprehensive performance of airway prediction.
DBR, DLR aim to assess the topological continuity of airway prediction.
Running time aims to evaluate computational complexity.
"Lo P, Van Ginneken B, Reinhardt J M, et al. Extraction of airways from CT (EXACT'09)[J]. IEEE Transactions on
Medical Imaging, 2012, 31(11): 2093-2107."
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

Final Rank = Rank[Avg(IoU+Precision+DBR+DLR)]*0.6 + Rank[Running time]*0.2+Rank[Airway leakage]*0.2


We will use the“rank-then-aggrate” for ranking to provide a statistical significance assessment via challengeR
https://github.com/wiesenfa/challengeR

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

All mask predictions should be submitted after conducting the largest component extraction. The missing results
will be regarded as a failed prediction with 0 IoU, precision, DBR, DLR, and 1.0 leakages. The Running time for
failed cases will not be included in the overall running time.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

A well-performed model should perform well on completeness and continuity, with appropriate computational
complexity.

Average accuracy

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

The average accuracy of mortality status over different time periods shows the preliminary performance of
mortality prediction.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

Final Rank = Rank[Average accuracy of mortality status prediction].


We will use the“rank-then-aggrate” for ranking to provide a statistical significance assessment via challengeR
https://github.com/wiesenfa/challengeR

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

The missing results will be regarded as a failed prediction.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

The accuracy straightly reflects the performance of the prognosis model.
